$commentDropped: CORRECTION 2026-08-28: Mistral was removed on 2026-08-27 for "console.mistral.ai did not resolve" and that verdict was WRONG. The host is alive and answers 302; the checker followed an endless login redirect between console.mistral.ai, auth.mistral.ai and v2.auth.mistral.ai - a cookie-less client can never settle it - and reported the resulting `fetch failed` as a dead link. Mistral is back below, and check-provider-links.mjs now treats a redirect loop as a login wall rather than a 404.
$comment: Providers with a genuine free tier, curated. Every `id` is a real id in the gateway's own provider manifest (GET /api/v1/provider-plugin-manifest, 222 providers), so `omni-agent provider add <id>` resolves the base URL and auth mechanics from the gateway rather than from anything hardcoded here. `signup` is where a person goes to get the credential; those URLs are checked by scripts/check-provider-links.mjs and must not be shipped dead. `gives` is what the provider itself advertises - it is their claim, not a measurement, and the UI says so.
$commentRetired: GitHub Models was about to be added here on 2026-08-28 and was NOT, because it is retired. https://models.github.ai/inference/chat/completions answers HTTP 410 {"code":"github_models_retirement_brownout"} and GitHub's own docs say it was fully retired on 2026-07-30 - playground, catalogue, inference API and BYOK. The gateway's manifest still carries `github-models` (alias `ghm`, apikey) and OmniRoute's Free-tiers page still advertises it, so BOTH are stale: a provider being in the manifest is not evidence that it works. GitHub Copilot is a different thing and is still live - it is the `github` OAuth entry under signIn, and it needs a paid seat.

models.label: Pollinations
models.gives: GPT, Llama and Claude-class models with no account at all
models.note: Nothing to sign up for. Add it and it works.

models.label: Cerebras
models.gives: Free credits to start, and the fastest inference on this list
models.note: Free credits, no card. Verified on their pricing page 2026-08-27. Best single addition for speed.

models.label: Mistral
models.gives: Mistral Large, Small and Codestral, on whatever their current free tier allows
models.note: Signed out, the console bounces you through auth.mistral.ai before showing a login. That is normal - it is not a broken link.
setup: Open https://console.mistral.ai/ and sign in. Signed out it redirects through auth.mistral.ai first - that is their login flow, not a broken link.
Read their plan page before you pick one. Mistral's free tier has changed more than once and their page is the authority on what it currently includes.
Open 'API Keys' in the console's left-hand menu and create a key.
Run:  omni-agent provider add mistral YOUR-KEY
Its models then appear in the app's model picker under 'From your keys'.

models.label: Groq
models.gives: A free tier on Llama, Qwen and GPT-OSS models
models.note: Very fast. Rate-limited per minute rather than per month.

models.label: OpenCode Zen
models.note: Free forever. This is the pool the agent already uses by default.

models.label: Kilo Code
models.gives: An auto-router plus Tencent Hy3, free
models.note: Sign in with your account instead of pasting a key.

models.label: SiliconFlow
models.gives: DeepSeek V3.2 and R1 on a free tier

models.label: Cloudflare Workers AI
models.gives: 50+ models on a free daily allowance
models.note: Needs a Cloudflare account ID as well as a token.

models.label: NVIDIA NIM
models.gives: GLM and MiniMax on a free rate-limited tier

models.label: OpenRouter
models.gives: Every model tagged :free, and higher limits if you ever top up
models.note: The widest single catalogue. Free models are rate-limited, not metered.

models.label: Google Gemini
models.gives: A free tier on Gemini Flash models
models.note: Google publishes no quota API, so usage will read as unavailable.

models.label: Chutes
models.gives: Open-weight models on a free allowance

$commentSignIn: Providers you do not pay extra for because you ALREADY pay for them. Signing in routes the agent through a subscription the user is holding anyway. These are OAuth in the gateway's manifest.
$commentSearch: Web search keys. These are NOT gateway providers - they are used by this product's own search tool, and are stored in the local encrypted credential store. Free tiers here remove the throttling that keyless search hits.

search.label: Brave Search
search.gives: Free credits every month on an independent web index
search.note: Independent index - it does not fail when Google or Bing do. Verified 2026-08-27.
setup: Open https://brave.com/search/api/ and pick the 'Search' plan, then 'Get started'.
Create a Brave account, or sign in if you have one.

The Search plan is billed at $5 per 1,000 requests and includes $5 of free credit EVERY MONTH, applied automatically - so roughly a thousand free searches a month, renewing. (Read from their pricing page on 2026-08-27; check it yourself, prices move.)
In the developer dashboard, create a subscription token. That token is your API key.
Run:  omni-agent provider add brave YOUR-KEY

search.label: Tavily
search.gives: A free monthly allowance, built for agents
search.note: Returns cleaned page content rather than just links, which suits research work.
setup: Open https://app.tavily.com/ and sign up (Google or GitHub sign-in works).
The API key is shown on the dashboard as soon as the account exists. It usually begins 'tvly-'.
Run:  omni-agent provider add tavily YOUR-KEY

search.label: Serper
search.gives: A one-time free grant of Google results
search.note: Google's results. The free grant does NOT renew, so keep it for work that needs Google specifically.
setup: Open https://serper.dev/ and sign up.
A free credit grant is added to the account automatically. It is one-time, not monthly.
Copy the API key from the dashboard.
Run:  omni-agent provider add serper YOUR-KEY

search.label: Firecrawl
search.gives: A free allowance of page scrapes
search.note: Scraping, not search. Only used as the last escalation when a page defeats both a plain fetch and the bundled browser.
setup: Open https://firecrawl.dev/ and sign up.
Copy the API key from the dashboard. It usually begins 'fc-'.
Run:  omni-agent provider add firecrawl YOUR-KEY
This one changes scraping, not search, so `omni-agent doctor` will not show it in the Web search row.

$commentGives: `gives` is deliberately QUALITATIVE. It used to carry specific allowances copied from OmniRoute's README and they did not survive checking on 2026-08-27: Cerebras was listed as '1M tokens/day' and its own pricing page says $5 in free credits; Brave was listed as '2,000 searches a month' and its own page says $5 in free monthly credits. Allowances change and a stale number shown to a non-technical user is worse than no number, so the signup page is the authority and this field only says what KIND of thing you get.
$commentKeyless: Search works with no key at all. These need no setup and are listed so the CLI can say so rather than leaving a user wondering what they are missing.

keyless.label: DuckDuckGo
keyless.note: Default. Throttles a machine that searches in bursts, which is why a key helps.

keyless.label: Brave (public page)
keyless.note: Brave's own index without a key. Independent of DuckDuckGo, so it does not fail at the same moment.

keyless.label: SearXNG
keyless.note: Public volunteer instances, tried in rotation.
setup: Nothing is required - a rotation of public instances is used automatically.
To stop depending on volunteers, point it at your own instance:
setx SEARXNG_INSTANCE https://my-searxng.example.com
Then restart the agent. One instance you control removes almost all search throttling.

keyless.label: Bundled browser
keyless.note: Last resort. Runs the search in the real Chromium this product already ships. Slower, but survives plain-HTTP endpoints being throttled.
